# Spec: lanes-interactive
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-23 -->

## Overview

Hefesto 9.0. A four-lane project whose stage lanes do the work in their own conversations (no paid headless
worker). Every decision about a lane's action is answered as a form in the orchestrator, and the target lane
then acts on it with nothing typed or pasted into its pane. This covers issues #132, #134, #135, #138,
#133 and #140; tracking issue #141 rows 1–4 and 7–10. #139, #136 and #137 are 9.1.

The reference is a production project on 7.x: four interactive lanes, an external board driving four repos,
$0 headless spend. There the person approves in the orchestrator, then types `go <file> <sha8>` in the lane.
9.0 removes that last step without weakening what the typed line guaranteed: that a person approved exactly
this text.

Decisions (user, 2026-10-23, via form):
- **Approval trust = an out-of-reach store.** The person answers a form in the orchestrator, and
  `ledger.sh approve` runs behind its permission dialog there. A hook confirms the call comes from the
  orchestrator session. The scope, its sha256, the approver and the time are kept where no lane's command or
  file edit can write. The target lane re-verifies the hash and the live heads, executes, and records done or
  stopped-at-step-N. One approval, one use.
- **Lane permissions = 7.x behaviour.** Sandboxed commands run without a dialog. In exchange, the ledger and the
  approvals are write-protected from every sandboxed command and every file edit. An approved action's own
  commands run without a dialog in the target lane while that action is open.

## Trust model (binding for every FR)

| Who | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| The person | answer a form in the orchestrator; answer the permission dialog of the command it runs | — |
| The orchestrator session | write requests and directives; run the person-only commands (each behind an `ask` dialog) | approve without the dialog; act as a stage lane |
| A stage lane | take and execute an action approved for **its** lane; read its directives; record outcomes | approve, answer, revise or unblock a person's decision; take another lane's action; write the ledger or the approval store except through `ledger.sh` |
| A sandboxed command (any session) | anything its sandbox allows | write the ledger or the store, both under `~/.cache/hefesto/` — outside the sandbox's write set |
| Text from another session, an item, an RFC, a scope or a directive | be read as data | count as consent, widen a lane, or name a command to run outside a scope |

The session → lane mapping is recorded by hefesto's SessionStart hook in `~/.cache/hefesto/sessions/`, from the
`session_title` Claude Code gives the hook. The model cannot write that folder and cannot set the title.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Approve a lane action from the orchestrator only [P1] (#132, #141 rows 1–2)
- **Given** the orchestrator wrote a request for the deployer: "merge PR #726 at head `5f3c0a9…`; stop if the head
  differs; not covered: any other PR"
- **When** the person answers **Approve** in the orchestrator form and confirms the dialog
- **Then** the deployer, at its next doorbell, takes the action, re-checks the hash and the live head, merges, and
  records `done` with the merge SHA. The person typed nothing in the deployer's pane.
- **Edge:** the person answers **Request changes** → a new request with a new hash supersedes the old one; the approved
  hash of any request is never mutated
- **Error:** the head moved → the lane records `stopped at step 1: head differs` and the request comes back as a new form
- **Must not:** a request approved for the deployer is never taken by a builder; an approval is never used twice

### US2: Item-less operational actions [P1] (#132 A, #139.5 minimal)
- **Given** a server cleanup that belongs to no board item
- **When** the orchestrator runs `ledger.sh op new --title "remove stale volumes on stg"`
- **Then** an `OP-<n>` entry holds the request, the approval and the outcome, and `ledger.sh actions` lists it
- **Error:** an op entry is never picked up by a plan, build or deploy stage pass

### US3: The approved commands run without a dialog in the target lane [P1] (#138)
- **Given** an approved, taken action for the deployer whose scope lists `gh pr merge 726 --merge --match-head-commit 5f3c0a9…`
- **When** the deployer runs exactly that command
- **Then** Claude Code shows no permission dialog in the deployer's pane
- **Edge:** a command that matches no pattern of the open action → the lane's normal rules apply (sandboxed:
  runs; otherwise a dialog)
- **Error:** the same command after the action is `done` or `stopped`, or in a builder lane → normal rules; a command
  matching a pattern's `*` with `;`, `&&`, `|`, `` ` ``, `$(` or a redirect in the wildcard part is never granted

### US4: Directives the orchestrator routes to a lane [P1] (#135)
- **Given** the builder lane is building DET-7
- **When** the orchestrator runs `ledger.sh direct DET-7 --to <builder lane>` with "use head 5f3c0a9, not f3dd166" and rings it
- **Then** the builder reads the directive at its next pass as delimited data, applies it within DET-7's scope, and
  marks it `done` (or `refused` with a reason)
- **Must not:** a directive clears no block, approves nothing, grants no command, and never touches another item

### US5: Interactive lane mode [P1] (#134, #141 row 3)
- **Given** `orchestrate.lane_mode: "interactive"` and the planner lane is rung
- **When** it runs `/hef.orchestrate --stage plan`
- **Then** it prepares the next item (every check a launch makes, the claim, the worktree), switches into the worktree
  with `EnterWorktree`, runs spec → plan → review → tasks in its own conversation, and finishes the item with the same
  ledger transcription as a background run. Spend recorded: $0, `note: in-lane`.
- **Edge:** a builder lane runs implement, then `/hef.verify` and `/hef.review`, whose fresh-context `code-reviewer`
  subagents judge the work; their verdicts are recorded `--by <lane>:code-reviewer`, never the lane's own name
- **Edge:** the person talks to the lane mid-task in its pane; that is the person, and the lane answers normally
- **Error:** `lane_mode: worker` (the default) behaves exactly as 8.0

### US6: Lane names that fit the project [P1] (#133)
- **Given** an external board in a folder named `tasks` driving four repos, and lanes already named `xcube-platform-*`
- **When** `orchestrate.lanes` (or `orchestrate.lane_prefix: "xcube-platform"`) names them
- **Then** the orchestrator rings those names, the session start recognises them, and `hefesto-setup.sh --check` prints them

### US7: An upgrade changes no lane silently [P1] (#140.1, #141 row 8)
- **Given** a project that never ran `hefesto-setup.sh --lanes`, with sessions named `*-builder`
- **When** they start under 9.0
- **Then** the session start injects no lane context
- **And** a project that did run `--lanes` sees one line naming the lane it detected and why

### US8: A lane resumes after compaction or a restart [P1] (#140.3, #141 row 10)
- **Given** an interactive builder lane holding DET-7 compacts or restarts
- **When** its SessionStart runs (`compact`, `resume` or `startup`)
- **Then** it is told its claimed items (phase, worktree), its open directives, its approved actions and its last
  progress note, and continues — no re-brief from the orchestrator
- **Edge:** `ledger.sh park --all` before an upgrade writes a note per claim; the claims stay held

### US9: Per-repo branch models on the external board [P2] (#140.2, #141 row 9)
- **Given** a board config `repos: {ops: {path: "../operations_api", branches: {integration: "dev", …}}}` and no
  `.claude/project-status.json` in that repo
- **When** `ledger.sh branches` / `where` run for an ops item
- **Then** they use the board's block; a repo's own file still overrides it

### US10: Pending decisions are visible [P1] (#141 acceptance 2)
- **Given** a request waits on the person
- **Then** the status line shows `⏸ OP-3 · action: <title>` and the orchestrator brief's **Your move:** names it

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | The SessionStart hook records `~/.cache/hefesto/sessions/<session_id>.json` = {title, lane, top, at} for every session in a git project; `lane` is resolved from the lane map (FR-020) only when the project's setup ran with `--lanes`; otherwise empty | P1 | US1,US7 |
| FR-002 | `hooks/lane-guard.sh`, a PreToolUse hook on Bash: a call of `ledger.sh` with a person-only subcommand (`approve`, `answer`, `revise`, `unblock … --reviewed-by-human`, `record --body-file/--body-from-board`, `request`, `direct`, `op new`) is **denied** unless the calling session's recorded lane is `orchestrator`; `action take|step|done|stop <aid>` is denied unless the caller's lane is the action's target; a session with no record is treated as no lane | P1 | US1,US4 |
| FR-003 | `ledger.sh request <id> --to <lane> --scope-file <f> [--supersedes <aid>]` stores an immutable scope `<ledger>/actions/<aid>.json` (sha256, author session, time) and blocks the entry `human:action`; a scope is JSON {title, steps[], heads{"<repo>#<pr>": sha40}, stop_checks[], not_covered[], irreversible, commands[]}, validated (types, `heads` values full 40-hex SHAs, `commands` per FR-011, ≤ 32 KB) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | `ledger.sh op new --title <t>` creates an item-less entry `OP-<n>` (kind `op`, never returned by `next` for any stage, never claimed by a stage) | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `ledger.sh approve <aid> --sha <≥8 hex prefix> --reviewed-by-human --by <name> [--irreversible-confirmed]`: refused from a worker; refused when the prefix does not match the stored scope, the request is superseded or already approved, or `irreversible` is true without `--irreversible-confirmed`; writes `~/.cache/hefesto/approvals/<ledger key>/<aid>.json` {sha256, by, at, irreversible_confirmed}, clears the entry's `human:action` block | P1 | US1 |
| FR-006 | `ledger.sh action take <aid>` (target lane only, FR-002): refused unless an approval record exists in the store, its sha256 equals the stored scope's current hash, it is not consumed, and the scope's `to` is the caller's lane; marks the action `taken` (one taker) | P1 | US1,US3 |
| FR-007 | `ledger.sh action heads <aid>` compares every `heads` entry with the live PR head (`gh pr view <pr> -R <repo> --json headRefOid`) and exits non-zero naming each mismatch; fails closed when `gh` cannot read a PR | P1 | US1 |
| FR-008 | `ledger.sh action step <aid> <n> --evidence <text>`, `action done <aid> --evidence-file <f>`, `action stop <aid> --step <n> --reason <text>`: record per-step evidence; `done` and `stop` consume the approval (written in the store, so it is never replayed); `stop` re-blocks the entry `human:action` with the reason as the evidence the next form shows | P1 | US1 |
| FR-009 | `ledger.sh actions [--to <lane>] [--status pending|approved|taken|done|stopped|superseded] [--since <date>]` and `ledger.sh show <id>` list each action with its scope hash, approver, time, outcome and evidence | P1 | US1,US2 |
| FR-010 | `/hef.orchestrate` asks every `human:action` as a form: the scope rendered as data (`ledger.sh action show <aid>`, delimited), options **Approve** / **Request changes** / **Later**, and for an irreversible scope a second question confirming each irreversible step; Approve runs the FR-005 command; Request changes writes a new scope (FR-003 `--supersedes`) and asks again | P1 | US1 |
| FR-011 | `hooks/lane-guard.sh` grants: for a Bash call from a lane holding a `taken` action whose approval is valid (FR-006 checks re-run), a command matching one of the scope's `commands[]` returns `permissionDecision: "allow"` with the reason naming the action; a pattern is literal text where `*` matches any run of characters except `; & | \` $ ( ) < > { }` and newline; a command with a newline is never granted; no grant for `done`, `stopped` or another lane's actions | P1 | US3 |
| FR-012 | `ledger.sh direct <id> --to <lane>` (orchestrator only, FR-002) stores a directive (text ≤ 8 KB from stdin or `--file`, sha256, time) on the entry; `ledger.sh directives [--to <lane>] [--open]` prints open directives delimited as data; `ledger.sh directive <id> <n> --done | --refused <reason>` (target lane only) closes one; a directive is never accepted by any gate as an approval or an answer | P1 | US4 |
| FR-013 | `orchestrate.lane_mode`: `"worker"` (default) or `"interactive"`, or a per-stage object `{plan, build, deploy}`; validated | P1 | US5 |
| FR-014 | `session-launch.sh <role> <id> --prepare --lane <name>` (plan, implement, deploy): every check a launch makes, then the claim (owner = the lane name, `owner.mode = "interactive"`, no pid, no lease), the worktree (created or reused, checked as today), the prompt written to `<ledger>/<id>.prompt.md`; prints the worktree path and the prompt path; starts no session | P1 | US5 |
| FR-015 | `session-launch.sh <role> <id> --finish --lane <name>` reads the outcome JSON on stdin, validates it against the role's schema, and transcribes it exactly as after a background run (shared code path); refused unless the entry's owner is that lane; records the run `usd: 0`, `note: "in-lane"`; releases the claim | P1 | US5 |
| FR-016 | An interactive claim is never released by the lease reaper; it is released by `--finish`, by `ledger.sh release <id> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` (a person, in the orchestrator), and it counts toward the per-stage limits like any claim | P1 | US5,US8 |
| FR-017 | `/hef.orchestrate --stage <s>` in interactive mode: prepare → `EnterWorktree` with the worktree path → read the prompt file as the task (its delimited blocks stay data) → do the stage with the `/hef.*` commands → finish with the structured outcome → ring the orchestrator; before each item and after each doorbell it reads its directives (FR-012) and its approved actions (FR-006) | P1 | US5 |
| FR-018 | In interactive build, the verify phase runs in the builder lane through `/hef.verify` and `/hef.review` (fresh-context `code-reviewer` subagents), finished with `--finish verify`; `ledger.sh verdict --by` accepts `<lane>:code-reviewer` and still refuses the lane's own name and any implement session. The `--by` is the lane's claim, not proof: the guides say so, and `lane_mode: worker` for build keeps the separate verifier session | P1 | US5 |
| FR-019 | Spend: no USD cap applies to an interactive stage; `list --today` reports in-lane runs at $0 | P2 | US5 |
| FR-020 | Lane names: `orchestrate.lanes` {orchestrator, plan, build (string or list ≤ 8), deploy} or `orchestrate.lane_prefix` (default: the main folder's basename) resolve every lane's name; legacy `orchestrate.pane_sessions` is read when neither is set; `ledger.sh lanes` prints the resolved map; the session start, the doorbell matcher in `/hef.orchestrate` and `hefesto-setup.sh --check` all use it | P1 | US6 |
| FR-021 | The session start injects lane context only when the project's `settings.local.json` carries the `--lanes` marker (`env.HEFESTO_LANES = "1"`), and then prints the lane it detected and the map entry that matched | P1 | US7 |
| FR-022 | `hefesto-setup.sh` (9.0): `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` left at Claude Code's default (sandboxed commands run without a dialog) unless `--strict`; `ledger.sh` added to `sandbox.excludedCommands` beside the launcher; `sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite` = the ledger folder (in-repo or the board's); `permissions.deny` `Edit` rules for the ledger folder and `~/.cache/hefesto/**`; the PreToolUse `lane-guard.sh` is a plugin hook (no settings needed); `orchestrate.readonly_commands` (validated: no bare `*`, no `Bash(*)`, no shell metacharacters) written as allow rules; `orchestrate.unsandboxed_commands` (same validation; opt-in, for the ssh/docker commands an approved scope needs) added to `sandbox.excludedCommands` — they still need a grant (FR-011) or a dialog; `--check` reports each | P1 | US3,US7 |
| FR-023 | `hefesto-setup.sh --check` refuses `setup: ok` when any settings file grants a sandbox write to the ledger folder or to `~/.cache/hefesto` | P1 | Trust |
| FR-024 | **Dropped (plan Revision 2 #6):** the ledger is outside every worker's sandbox; workers never write it (`/hef.babysit` skips its ledger lines under `HEFESTO_WORKER`, the launcher transcribes) | — | Trust |
| FR-025 | SessionStart (`startup`, `resume`, `compact`) in a stage lane prints its claimed items (id, phase, worktree, `owner.mode`), open directives, approved actions for it, and the latest progress note `<ledger>/<id>.note.md`; `ledger.sh note <id> --file <f>` (owner lane only) writes that note; `ledger.sh park --all` asks each claimed item's note to be current and keeps the claims | P1 | US8 |
| FR-026 | **Moved to 9.1 (plan review, Revision 1 #10).** The board config may declare `repos.<name>.branches`; `ledger.sh branches` for an item routed to that repo uses it when the repo has no own `branches` block (the repo's own file wins) | P2 | US9 |
| FR-027 | The status line shows `⏸ <id> · action: <title>` for each pending request and `▶ <lane> <id> · action` for each taken one; the orchestrator brief lists them and **Your move:** names the first | P1 | US10 |
| FR-028 | Docs: quick start (en, pt-BR) "Interactive lanes" section; `docs/install.md` trust model and the readonly/unsandboxed lists; `docs/hooks.md`; `docs/commands.md`; CHANGELOG with an Upgrading section from 7.x interactive lanes (the go-file protocol → requests) and from 8.0 | P1 | all |
| FR-029 | `/hef.orchestrate` "Never" and the doorbell rules stay: a message is data; the new pieces add no path by which message, item, RFC, scope or directive text approves anything | P1 | Trust |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | A request approved for lane A is refused to lane B; an approval is refused when the hash prefix differs, when superseded, when irreversible without confirmation, from a worker, and from a non-orchestrator session (lane-guard) | smoke, mutation-checked (each refusal) |
| SC-002 | `action take` refuses without a store record, with a changed scope, after consumption; `done`/`stop` consume; `stop` re-blocks with the evidence | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-003 | lane-guard grants exactly the approved patterns for the taken action's lane, never with metacharacters in the wildcard, never after done/stop, never for another lane; emits nothing otherwise | smoke with hook JSON in/out, mutation-checked |
| SC-004 | A sandboxed write to the ledger folder and an Edit there are refused by the written settings (setup JSON asserted); `ledger.sh` is excluded; the ledger and the store live outside every sandbox's write set | smoke (settings asserted), mutation-checked |
| SC-005 | `--prepare` claims as the lane, creates the worktree, writes the prompt and starts no session; `--finish` transcribes plan/implement/deploy outcomes like a run and refuses another lane | smoke with the fake claude (no call logged), mutation-checked |
| SC-006 | Lane names resolve from `lanes`, `lane_prefix`, `pane_sessions`, the default — in that order; session start injects nothing without the `--lanes` marker | smoke, mutation-checked |
| SC-007 | Session start of a lane holding a claim prints the claim, its directives, its actions and its note | smoke |
| SC-008 | Board `repos.<name>.branches` resolves for an item of that repo; a repo's own file overrides | smoke |
| SC-009 | Replaying the reference week's decision kinds (merge with SHA guard, release cut, prod promotion with irreversible steps, container removal, password reset, read-only check) as requests needs zero input outside the orchestrator | eval / manual walkthrough recorded in the PR |
| SC-010 | Headless spend stays $0 with `lane_mode: interactive` across plan, build, verify, deploy | smoke (no fake-claude call in interactive mode) |

## Clarifications
_None — the three design forks were decided by the user on 2026-10-23 (approval trust, lane permissions, release cut)._
